01 Executive Summary and Final Classification

Final classification: Watchlist — Mixed Temporal Evidence. Negative 5D Momentum was supported by exploration and passed a frozen temporal validation. The single final held-out test did not meet the predeclared evidence threshold. The research is closed; the original hypothesis and result are preserved. [R1, R7, R8, R9]

Final primary metricRecorded value

The mean remains negative, but p ≥ 0.05 and the upper confidence bound is above zero. Failure to reject the null does not prove a zero effect or establish equivalence. It does mean that the predefined final evidence standard for a robust predictive candidate was not met.

02 Economic Motivation and Mathematical Definition

The original implementation is unchanged and defaults to a 20-day lookback. The investigated candidate and both frozen tests use L = 5. Prices are adjusted daily Close; periods count observed trading rows, not calendar days. No missing-price filling is performed. [R1, R2, R8]

ML(t)=PtPt−L−1

Investigated orientation: S(t) = −M₅(t). Target: R(t) = P[t+6] / P[t+1] − 1.

Continuation is the natural hypothesis for positively oriented raw Momentum. The observed short-horizon negative relationship instead motivates a reversal interpretation: recent relative losers outperform winners. Temporary price pressure, liquidity provision and overreaction are possible explanations, not identified causal mechanisms. Negating the signal is an orientation convention and supplies no new evidence. Frozen tests retain raw Momentum and the alternative mean IC < 0.

03 Dataset and Research Methodology

The original 300-security universe was deterministically selected from current S&P 500 constituents with sector coverage. The adjusted Yahoo Finance snapshot and current sector metadata are frozen; the sample is not historical index membership. Exploration covers 2010–2016; frozen validation covers 2017–2019; the single final test covers 2020–2025. #001-B and #001-C subsequently reused 2010–2019 as post-validation exploration. [R2–R8]

Saved #001-C coverage diagnostics; pooled and subperiod rows overlap
PeriodUniversePrice coverageRaw IC datesRisk common datesMean common pairs
2010–201930089.39%25052450267.78
2010–201630087.91%17511696263.27
2017–201930092.85%748748277.94

Daily Spearman IC uses aligned signal-date/ticker pairs, average ranks for ties, at least 100 pairs and nonconstant cross sections. Means equally weight eligible dates; dispersion uses sample SD (ddof = 1); ICIR is unannualized mean/SD. Available samples differ by specification. Strict common samples intersect paired assets before recomputing ranks and then intersect valid dates.

Labels are bounded independently within each reported period. Up to 60 pre-period rows warm longer controls where available; no pre-2010 history exists in the snapshot. The final protocol uses exactly five pre-2020 rows. Its last six signal rows lack in-boundary exits and are excluded. Missing endpoints remain undefined; no synthetic prices are introduced.

05 Lookback and Prediction Horizon Analysis

Fixed L ∈ {5,20,60}, H ∈ {5,10,20,60}, entry lag 1. #001-B is explicitly post-validation exploration; 2017–2019 was already seen. The pooled 5D cumulative mean IC attenuates from −0.015404 at H=5 to −0.007776 at H=60. In 2017–2019, 60D Momentum has positive cumulative means across the fixed horizons, while 20D changes sign at H=60. No optimum is selected. Detailed saved summary statistics appear in the appendix. [R3]

07 Sector and Volatility Risk Controls

Realized volatility is the unannualized sample SD of complete trailing 20/60 daily simple returns ending on the signal date. Daily neutralization fits Momentum on sector dummies, separately with vol20, vol60 or both, before filtering future labels. Regressions of raw future returns on Momentum and controls use outcome-complete samples. No present-day capitalization was used. Conditional linear slopes and Spearman IC measure different relationships. [R5]

10 Final Research Assessment and Alpha Signal Implications

Watchlist — Mixed Temporal Evidence; Research Status: Closed. The pre-test Alpha Candidate assessment remains an unchanged historical record. The final assessment is the current classification. The unmet frozen final threshold prevents calling this a confirmed robust predictive candidate, while non-rejection does not prove no relationship. [R8, R9]

Evidence levelWhat this archive supports
Predictive associationNegative sample mean IC in exploration, validation and final periods; the final test did not reject its null.
Incremental informationDescriptive residual association under limited sector/volatility controls on already-seen data.
Tradable AlphaNot established; costs, execution, capacity and comprehensive risk-adjusted performance were not tested.

The final quantile shape is not strictly monotonic. Any interpretation of nonlinearity or regime differences after the final result is a post-test observation, not confirmatory evidence. No new model, subgroup, horizon or replacement hypothesis is fitted. The original test must not be repeated or resealed. Closure authorizes no new factor study.

11 Limitations and Reproducibility

Current-constituent selection creates survivorship and selection bias; frozen sector labels are not historical point-in-time classifications. IPO availability, absent delisted histories, missing endpoints, vendor revisions and retrospective corporate-action adjustments remain limitations. Complete-case/common samples condition on availability, and no prices were filled. [R2–R9]

Overlapping labels, shared securities and persistent signals induce dependence. Lag-5 HAC is not a guarantee against longer dependence and was not automatically reused for longer horizons. Exploratory windows, sectors, regimes, groups, horizons and controls create multiple comparisons; reused samples are not independent replications. No new multiplicity correction or significance test is performed in this publication.

Historical beta, size, value, quality, liquidity and event exposures remain incompletely controlled. No turnover, bid-ask costs, financing, short availability, capacity or implementable portfolio constraints were evaluated. Positive quantile labels can include market exposure and cannot be compounded as overlapping strategy performance.

This publication reads saved summaries and embeds original figures; no market-price panel is parsed. Existing integrity routines hash original bytes and check pinned versions only. HTML and PDF are built from identical content. Embedded PNGs, CSS and native MathML require no network. See the accompanying README and publication_manifest.json for build commands, hashes and QA. The source records remain authoritative; publication rounding is presentation only.
